Package com.egradx.auth.account

Class EgradxEmailChangeService

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.auth.account.EgradxEmailChangeService
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.beans.factory.Aware, org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisherAware
public class EgradxEmailChangeService extends Object implements org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisherAware
Changing the address you sign in with.

Starting needs the current password; a six-digit code then goes to the new address, and the change happens only once that code is entered — proving the person can read mail there. The old address is told afterwards, so a hijacked session changing it does not go unnoticed. A username that was the old address follows it to the new one. Sessions carry on: nothing about the password changed.

    • confirm

      @Transactional(noRollbackFor=ValidationException.class) public EgradxUserDto confirm(UUID userId, String code)
      Completes the change with the code sent to the new address. A wrong code counts against the limit, and that count is kept even though an exception is thrown — hence noRollbackFor.
      Throws:
      ValidationException - EMAIL_CHANGE_NOT_STARTED, EMAIL_CHANGE_EXPIRED, EMAIL_CHANGE_INVALID_CODE, EMAIL_CHANGE_TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS
      DuplicateResourceException - EMAIL_IN_USE — taken by someone else in the meantime
